t: From about 1600 BCE warrior chiefs on the Greek mainland grew rich, as the gold of the shaft graves at Mycenae shows, and by 1400 BCE kings ruled palace states at Mycenae, Pylos, Thebes and elsewhere.
Their scribes wrote Linear B, deciphered in 1952 as the earliest known form of Greek, to record land, livestock, workers, weapons and offerings to gods such as Zeus and Poseidon.
Around 1200 BCE the palaces were destroyed and writing was forgotten; Homer’s epics, composed centuries later, remember Mycenae as Agamemnon’s city, but they are evidence of memory, not of fact.
dyk: Zeus, Hera, Poseidon, Hermes and Dionysus are all named on Linear B tablets of about 1200 BCE from Pylos, the oldest written records of the Greek gods, some five centuries before Homer and Hesiod.
ev: Rich burials in the shaft graves of Mycenae mark the rise of a warrior elite
Mycenaean Greeks take over Knossos on Crete, where Linear B comes into use
The walls of Mycenae are extended and the Lion Gate is built
A Hittite king writes to the king of Ahhiyawa as his “brother” in the Tawagalawa letter
A wave of destruction ends the palaces; Pylos burns around 1180 BCE
The last Mycenaean communities fade as Greece enters the Early Iron Age
Heinrich Schliemann excavates the shaft graves of Grave Circle A at Mycenae
Michael Ventris deciphers Linear B, showing that it records Greek

f.homeland: Mainland Greece, above all the Peloponnese, Attica and Boeotia, with Crete from c. 1450 BCE, the Aegean islands, Rhodes and outposts such as Miletus on the coast of Anatolia (Greece and Turkey today)
f.period: c. 1600–1100 BCE; the shaft graves of Mycenae c. 1600–1500 BCE, the palace states c. 1400–1200 BCE, then destruction around 1200 BCE and a long decline
f.known: The citadels of Mycenae and Tiryns with their Cyclopean walls and the Lion Gate; the gold of the shaft graves; tholos tombs such as the Treasury of Atreus; the Linear B tablets, the oldest written Greek; the heroes of Homer’s epics
f.sources: Excavated citadels, palaces and tombs (Heinrich Schliemann at Mycenae from 1876, Carl Blegen at Pylos from 1939); Linear B tablets, deciphered by Michael Ventris in 1952; Hittite letters about Ahhiyawa and Egyptian lists of Aegean places; later Greek epic and myth, which preserve memories rather than history
